en.name: Plateau pressure (Pplat)
en.shortDescription: Plateau pressure (Pplat) — airway pressure during an end-inspiratory hold, in cmH2O.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Plateau pressure (Pplat) is the airway pressure at zero inspiratory flow, reflecting the pressure distending the alveoli — the elastic recoil of the lungs and chest wall. It is a key target in lung-protective ventilation (kept ≤ ~30 cmH2O). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar). The zero-flow condition is usually obtained with an end-inspiratory hold, but not always: in pressure-control modes where inspiratory flow decelerates to zero before the end of inspiration, the end-inspiratory pressure already is the plateau, and some ventilator pneumatics cannot perform a hold at all and derive the value instead. ## Included Concepts The set resolves to four concepts: three LOINC "Clinical Observation" codes and one SNOMED observable entity. - *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway (LOINC)*: the generic LOINC plateau pressure, context unspecified. The default. - *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same measurement, with the "on ventilator" context made explicit. - *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure (SNOMED)*: the SNOMED equivalent, for sources that carry no LOINC code. - *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure (LOINC)*: a plateau pressure obtained without a dedicated hold manoeuvre — see below. The two `Pressure.plateau` LOINC codes are pulled in through their shared LOINC Hierarchy anchor, which covers exactly these two and nothing else. *21490565 / 60802-6* sits on a separate branch and is listed explicitly. **Note on the "dynamic" concept.** LOINC publishes no definition for *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure*, and its component (`Pressure.plateau dynamic`) differs from the `Pressure.plateau` component of the other two LOINC codes. Its meaning comes from IEEE 11073-10101, of which it is an import: the code maps as `equivalent` to `MDC_PRESS_RESP_PLAT_DYNAMIC` (152776) in the LOINC/IEEE mapping table shipped with the LOINC release [1], where the term denotes the airway pressure that would have been observed during an inspiratory hold — a plateau obtained without performing one. Valveless ventilators do this by necessity: the HAMILTON-C1/T1/MR1 derive it as `(VTE / Cstat) + PEEP` and display it only when end-inspiratory flow is near zero [2]. All four concepts therefore describe the same physiological quantity and share the same unit, which is why they are kept in one set; what differs is how the zero-flow condition was reached. **Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar). ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records a plateau pressure (Pplat): *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway*. This is the generic LOINC code, and the one ventilators emit through the IEEE 11073 Rosetta respiratory panel. - **Source states the patient was on the ventilator**: *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator*. - **Source carries no LOINC code**: *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure* (SNOMED). - **Use *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure* only** when the source explicitly labels the value as obtained without a hold manoeuvre — a device field named for a dynamic or estimated plateau, or a ventilator model known not to perform holds. A plateau pressure of unknown provenance is **not** a reason to pick it: use the generic code above. - The four concepts belong in the same column. Where the distinction matters for an analysis — comparing a hold-derived value with a device-derived one — recover it from `measurement_concept_id`, not from the value. - Convert mbar to cmH2O (×1.02) before mapping. - **Not peak, mean or PEEP**: these are distinct pressures in their own concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC/IEEE Medical Device Code Mapping Table, distributed with the LOINC release (`AccessoryFiles/LoincIeeeMedicalDeviceCodeMappingTable`). Maps LOINC 60802-6 to IEEE 11073-10101 `MDC_PRESS_RESP_PLAT_DYNAMIC` (152776) as `equivalent`. Available: https://loinc.org/downloads/ [2] Hamilton Medical. Calculating Pplateau with HAMILTON-C1/T1/MR1 ventilators. Available: https://www.hamilton-medical.com/en_US/Resource-center/Article-page~knowledge-base~14232908-6f10-47d0-abe1-2e5b9de333f1~Calculating-Pplateau-with-HAMILTON-C1-T1-MR1-ventilators~.html
